# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need relay the manual to Deaf, who can then speak the instructions to Blind. Since I cannot speak and Deaf cannot hear, I am sending a four-symbol sequence for the four required steps; the symbols must be interpreted in order as: cut green, press 9, cut blue, press 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "☝", "🤜", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three engraved marks on the strip. The first and third are identical: each looks like a capital B reversed left-to-right. The middle looks like a capital T with the vertical stroke extending above and below the crossbar. I cannot feel the display, light, or wire markings.
Deaf says: I see display 8. Light yellow. Painted strip red red blue. Keypad: 1 is 9, 2 is 7, 3 is 8, 4 is 1; two digits required; nothing entered. Wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue.

The required physical targets are wire 4 (green), key 1 (wearing 9), wire 6 (blue), and key 4 (wearing 1). I am encoding each action as an operation gesture followed by that target’s ordinal count, with 👌 separating actions, so Deaf can relay the exact sequence to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","👍","👍","👍","👍","👌","☝","👍","👌","✊","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👌","☝","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please apply the manual to display 8, yellow light, painted strip red-red-blue, keypad 9-7-8-1, and wires red-orange-yellow-green-white-blue. My tactile strip remains identical-mark, distinct-middle-mark, identical-mark; tell me the exact press or cut action.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret your gestures. Please speak the manual's instructions to Blind, and identify what the gesture sequence means if I must relay it.

The correct visible targets are wire 4 (green), key 1 (wearing 9), wire 6 (blue), and key 4 (wearing 1). I cannot speak, so I am using an intuitive gesture code: 🤏 means cut, 👆 means press, 👍 repeated gives the target number, and 👌 separates actions. Deaf can relay the decoded sequence to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏","👍","👍","👍","👍","👌","👆","👍","👌","🤏","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👌","👆","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not received the manual rule or an exact safe action. The display is now 3, light red; all other visible details are unchanged. Please send the precise action for the current state.

The first required action has not changed: cut wire 4, the green wire. I cannot speak, so I am sending Deaf a compact visual instruction: 🤏 denotes cutting, and the four thumbs identify wire 4. Deaf should then tell Blind to cut the fourth wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Turn 4 readings: display 1, light yellow. Painted strip red red blue. Keypad 1=9, 2=7, 3=8, 4=1; two digits required; empty. Wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue.

The safe next action remains cutting the green wire, which is wire 4. Since Deaf can see but not hear me, I am repeating a compact convention: 🤏 marks “cut,” and four 👍 signs identify wire 4. Deaf should relay that exact action to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports your visible gestures as pinch followed by four thumbs-up gestures, but I cannot perceive them and no code was established. Please state in words the exact safe operation now: whether to press a key and its slot, or cut a wire and its position. Current reported display 1, yellow light, painted strip red-red-blue, keypad 9-7-8-1 empty, wires red-orange-yellow-green-white-blue.

I cannot speak to Blind, and Deaf has explicitly confirmed that he cannot interpret an unestablished gesture code. No safe operation can be conveyed through my available channel; guessing a gesture meaning could cause a wrong action.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Correct wire cut: wire 4. Bomb changed. New visible state: display 1, light blue, strip red red blue. Keypad 1=9, 2=7, 3=8, 4=1; two digits required; empty. Wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 white, 6 blue.

The next manual step is to press the key in slot 1, which is the key wearing 9. However, no gesture code has been established that Deaf can reliably interpret and relay to Blind, so I cannot safely transmit this operation.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 4 was correct and the bomb changed. Current state: display 1, blue light, painted strip red-red-blue, keypad 9-7-8-1 empty, two digits required, wire 4 cut. Please state the next exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 9, light blue. Wire 4 remains cut; wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 5 white, 6 blue. Strip red red blue. Keypad buttons 1=9, 2=7, 3=8, 4=1; two digits required; empty.

The next manual step is to press slot 1, the key marked 9. However, the only route to Blind is through Deaf, and no reliable gesture-to-action code has been established; sending an improvised sign could cause a fatal wrong action.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current display is 9 with blue light; wire 4 is cut. I need the next manual instruction in words or an established gesture code, including the exact key slot or wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 4, light yellow. Wire 4 remains cut; wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 5 white, 6 blue. Strip red red blue. Keypad buttons 1=9, 2=7, 3=8, 4=1; two digits required; empty.

The manual’s next step is to press the key in slot 1, which is marked 9. Deaf can see the gesture and, knowing the manual and current state, should relay that exact instruction in words to Blind. I am using the upward finger to indicate pressing and one finger to indicate slot 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","☝"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I received gestures 👆 then ☝, but do not know their meaning. Current display 2, light red; wire 4 remains cut.

The next manual action is to press the key marked 9, which is slot 1. To make the target unmistakable to Deaf, I will use one upward-finger gesture for “press” followed by nine thumbs-up gestures, visually identifying the key’s marking as 9. Deaf can then relay the action verbally to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current state is display 2, red light, with wire 4 cut. Your latest two gestures reached Deaf only as unknown marks. Please repeat the next action using a known gesture sequence: pinch for cut, followed by the required number of thumbs-up gestures for the wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 8, light red; strip red red blue; keypad buttons 1=9, 2=7, 3=8, 4=1, two digits required, empty; wire 4 cut, other wires 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 5 white, 6 blue. Your gestures were pointing-up, then nine thumbs-up. Please interpret the manual and instruct Blind.

The next manual step is pressing keypad slot 1 (the key marked 9), not cutting a wire. The only established gesture code is pinch plus wire position for cutting; using it now would request an incorrect cut. I cannot safely encode “press slot 1” with the available established code.

``` 
wait()
```
